title: "Export a Snowflake Baseline"
page-type: how-to
audience: "Authorized data engineers"

---

## Prerequisites

- A configured development environment.
- Authorized read access supplied through `SNOWFLAKE_*` environment variables or an uncommitted env file.
- A country code, storm identifier, and forecast time for the case.

## Steps

1. Preview the export without connecting or writing artifacts:

   ```bash
   uv run aots-report export-snowflake \
     --country <ISO3> \
     --storm <STORM_ID> \
     --forecast-time <FORECAST_TIME> \
     --case-name <CASE_NAME> \
     --env-file .env \
     --plan-only \
     --json
   ```

2. Review the non-secret plan, especially the target and filters.

3. Run the read-only export:

   ```bash
   uv run aots-report export-snowflake \
     --country <ISO3> \
     --storm <STORM_ID> \
     --forecast-time <FORECAST_TIME> \
     --case-name <CASE_NAME> \
     --env-file .env
   ```

4. Validate and regenerate from the exported baseline:

   ```bash
   SNAPSHOT_OUT="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/aots-export-check.XXXXXX")"
   uv run aots-report snapshot \
     --baseline "known-good-baselines/<CASE_NAME>" \
     --out "$SNAPSHOT_OUT"
   ```

## Expected Result

The exporter writes a validated Known-Good Baseline under `known-good-baselines/<CASE_NAME>` and prints the next snapshot command. The baseline contains `manifest.json`, `expected-report.json`, and role-grouped source artifacts.

## Safety Constraints

- Never place passwords or other secrets in CLI arguments, logs, fixtures, or committed files.
- The exporter is read-only against Snowflake and writes through a validated temporary sibling directory.
- It refuses a non-empty destination by default. Use `--overwrite` only after independently confirming that replacement is safe.
- Treat exported facility, beneficiary, geospatial, and operational data as local and sensitive.
